concept: JACCL ring all_reduce wire partitioning (n_wires, directions, threads)
summary: Ring all_reduce uses one direction and one wire when the message is 32768 bytes or less, or has fewer than `size * 2 * n_conns` elements; otherwise both directions and all wires

facts.text: Ring all_reduce uses one direction and one wire when the message is 32768 bytes or less, or has fewer than `size * 2 * n_conns` elements; otherwise both directions and all wires
The per-wire slice is `wire_offset[lr] = lr * n_wires * size_per_wire + lw * size_per_wire`, clamped to the wire's own end so frames cannot spill into the next wire
Ring all_gather and send/recv always use all `n_conns` wires with no small-message threshold
Ring sum_scatter uses one wire when `n_bytes <= 65536` or the element count is below `size * 2 * n_conns`
`RingGroup` allocates a `ThreadPool` of `n_conns - 1` workers and `dispatch_wires` runs the last wire inline on the calling thread
`RING_MAX_CONNS` is 4 per direction and the constructor throws above it
JACCL frames are 4096 bytes with 8 size classes, 2 buffers per class, 32 send and 32 receive work requests, pipeline depth 2
Ring buffer j maps to wire `j % n_conns` and direction `j / n_conns`, and is registered to that wire's own protection domain
`is_valid_ring` requires every neighbour pair to list as many devices as `devices_[0][1]`
Mesh `n_wires` is the minimum device count over all pairs, multi-wire starts at 512 KiB, and `MESH_MAX_PEERS` is 8
Mesh all_reduce uses reduce-scatter plus all-gather when size is above 2 and the per-wire bytes exceed 32 KiB, else a one-phase fully connected all_reduce
`init` prefers the ring only when `MLX_JACCL_RING` is set and the ring is valid, then falls back mesh, then ring
PR 3900 says the single-wire path has zero overhead because it runs in the calling thread
